topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestFlashblocksTransfer`
topIssues.author: wwared
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Reporting flaky test encountered across multiple CI runs.

## Test
`TestFlashblocksTransfer` in `github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-acceptance-tests/tests/flashblocks`

## CI Runs
- **op-geth variant (`memory-all-opn-op-geth`):** https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/121907/workflows/19d4587c-5b5a-4365-89be-097a41f59cb1/jobs/4751309
  - Branch: `aj/fix/build-kona-host` (pipeline 121907)
  - Exit code 1, runtime ~692s
- **op-reth variant (`memory-all-opn-op-reth`):** https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/121908/workflows/510d2c48-e61a-4974-a2b5-6786581baf72/jobs/4751415
  - Branch: `aj/fix/unskip-invalidblock-test` (pipeline 121908)
  - Exit code 1, runtime ~515s

## Date
2026-04-06

## Notes
- Failed on two different branches and two different execution clients (op-geth and op-reth), suggesting a non-deterministic issue in the test itself rather than in branch-specific code changes.
- The CI logs show the test running the full supernode/sequencer/batcher/proposer/challenger stack but the test ultimately fails without a clear assertion error visible in the truncated output.

topPRs.title: op-node, op-devstack: Test op-challenger super roots from op-node
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds acceptance-test coverage for op-challenger sourcing super roots from a single op-node (`superroot_atTimestamp`) instead of op-supernode, and fixes the one op-node gap that blocked it.

- New `dsl.SuperRootSource` interface (implemented by both op-supernode and op-node) makes the dispute-game DSL source-agnostic; `dsl.OpNodeSuperRoots` wraps an op-node. New `NewSingleChainInteropNoSupervisor` preset wires op-challenger to an op-node super-root source with no supervisor.
- `TestChallengerPlaysGameFromOpNode` — challenger counters a bad claim, op-node-sourced.
- `TestSingleChainSuperFaultProofsFromOpNode` — single-chain super-fault-proof smoke test (FPP + challenger trace provider), op-node-sourced.
- op-node's `superroot_atTimestamp` now clamps pre-genesis timestamps to the genesis super root, matching op-supernode. A fresh super dispute game's anchor is at timestamp 0; without this the challenger can't validate the game's starting anchor root against op-node and never plays the game.

## Test plan
Both acceptance tests pass locally (challenger 218s, smoke 43s). op-node superroot unit tests cover the pre-genesis clamp (`TestSuperrootAPI_PreGenesis`, `TestSuperrootAPI_TimestampZero_ClampsToGenesis`).

> Note: branched on the in-flight super-root-RPC-config rename work, so this PR currently also contains those 4 rename commits. The diff will narrow to just the test + op-node fix once those land on `develop`.

topPRs.title: docs: render the style guide as a site page in the Contribute nav group
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

## What / why

Follow-up to #21841 flagged during its review: `docs/public-docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md` was a repo-only file — invisible on docs.optimism.io and to `llms.txt`, which only indexes rendered pages. This PR renders it as a page in the Contribute nav group, next to the content guide it cross-links.

**Before:** The style guide lives only at `docs/public-docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md` on GitHub. Site visitors browsing the Contribute group can't find it, `llms.txt` consumers can't discover it, and two docs.json redirects (`/connect/contribute/style-guide`, `/reference/contribute/style-guide`) bounce readers out of the site to GitHub.

**After:** The style guide is served at `/op-stack/contribute/style-guide` in the **OP Stack ▸ Contribute** group alongside the content guide. The old redirects resolve inside the site. `DOCS_CONTRIBUTING.md` and the content guide's Next steps link to the rendered page.

## Single source of truth: move, not mirror

Per the render-vs-move decision required by the tracking issue, this is a **move**: `op-stack/contribute/style-guide.mdx` is now the canonical home, and `STYLE_GUIDE.md` is reduced to a pointer stub naming the `.mdx` source. Rationale:

- Mirroring would dual-source ~450 lines of prose — exactly what the [content guide's dual-sourcing ban](https://docs.optimism.io/op-stack/contribute/content-guide#link-dont-restate-the-dual-sourcing-ban) forbids ("requires double the effort to maintain and grows stale more quickly").
- Mintlify can't serve `STYLE_GUIDE.md` from the docs root — pages must live in the nav tree — so the `.md` file could never be the rendered source; the `.mdx` page has to exist either way, leaving "stub out the original" as the only zero-drift option.
- Precedent: the content guide (#21841) was born as an `.mdx` page under `op-stack/contribute/`; the style guide now sits beside it with the same `diataxis: reference` frontmatter.

The page content is a re-render of `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, not a rewrite: frontmatter added, the repo-file H1 dropped (Mintlify renders the frontmatter title), and repo-relative links adapted to site paths. Prose is otherwise unchanged.

## Changes

- New page: `docs/public-docs/op-stack/contribute/style-guide.mdx` (served at `/op-stack/contribute/style-guide`)
- `docs/public-docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md`: reduced to a pointer stub (site URL + `.mdx` source path)
- `docs/public-docs/docs.json`: **one nav addition** to the existing Contribute group, plus retargeting the two existing `/style-guide` redirects from GitHub to the new page — this PR holds the serialized docs.json slot
- `docs/public-docs/DOCS_CONTRIBUTING.md`: Style Guide link now points at the rendered page (with `.mdx` source pointer, matching the content-guide link pattern)
- `docs/public-docs/op-stack/contribute/content-guide.mdx`: Next steps style-guide link changed from the GitHub blob URL to `/op-stack/contribute/style-guide`

## Verification

- `docs.json` parses; every nav entry maps to an existing `.mdx`/`.md` file
- The new page compiles clean under MDX v3 (remark-gfm + frontmatter)
- `npx mint broken-links`: identical findings before and after this change (5 pre-existing broken links elsewhere in the tree, untouched) — no new findings
- No dead or circular pointers among `DOCS_CONTRIBUTING.md`, the content guide, the style-guide page, and the stub

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Page renders correctly in preview at `/op-stack/contribute/style-guide` (tables, blockquote examples, code fences)
- [ ] Nav placement (OP Stack ▸ Contribute, after Content guide) is acceptable
- [ ] Move-not-mirror decision (stub in `STYLE_GUIDE.md`) is acceptable as the single source of truth

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#966

topPRs.title: docs: add AI-native onboarding group (docs for AI/agents, MCP setup, prompt library)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784185257434409)_

## What / why

Option C (paved paths) **Slice 4 — AI-native onboarding group** (`ethereum-optimism/solutions`, `projects/docs-improver/plans/option-c-paved-paths.md`). The docs platform already serves machine-readable surfaces (llms.txt index, per-page markdown, a contextual copy/open-in-assistant menu configured in `docs.json`) — nothing on the site tells readers or agents about them. This PR surfaces those affordances as a small Get-Started-adjacent nav group with three new pages.

**Before:** an AI-assisted reader or agent has no on-site pointer to llms.txt or per-page markdown, no guidance for wiring the docs into an MCP-capable assistant, and no curated prompts — every assistant starts from scraped HTML and stale training data.

**After:** an "AI & Agents" group sits beside the Quickstart group with:

- `ai/docs-for-agents` — the machine-readable surfaces: the llms.txt index, `.md`-suffix per-page access, the contextual copy/open-in-ChatGPT/open-in-Claude menu, and grounding tips (specs are normative; re-check version-sensitive values).
- `ai/mcp-setup` — how to wire the docs into an MCP-capable assistant. No hosted MCP endpoint exists for docs.optimism.io today, so the page documents the llms.txt/markdown route (works with or without MCP) plus a reference fetch-server config; the hosted-MCP request is filed separately as ethereum-optimism/solutions#959 per the plan's fallback.
- `ai/prompt-library` — nine curated prompts mapped to the traced reader journeys (batcher cost audit, deposit flow, challenger deployment, node-stack choice, node setup, L1 bridging, fee estimation, Supersim, stuck withdrawal). Every entry names its persona (2 chain operator, 2 node operator, 5 app developer) and links at least one in-site page; entries will cross-link solution guides as later slices ship them. Carries `last-reviewed:` frontmatter per the plan's curation contract.

docs.json delta: one 8-line nav group, zero moves, zero redirects.

## Verification (lite accuracy pass)

- **Contextual-menu claim vs `docs.json`:** verified in-repo — `contextual.options` is exactly `["copy", "chatgpt", "claude"]` (docs.json lines 31–37 on this branch); the page describes exactly those three actions and no others.
- **In-site link targets:** all 20 unique in-site targets referenced across the three pages (markdown links + the `.md` URLs inside prompt blocks) verified to exist as `.mdx` files in the repo by script; link text checked against each target's frontmatter `title`.
- **Live URL resolution (llms.txt + per-page `.md`): could not be completed from this session — needs one human browser check before merge.** Attempted `https://docs.optimism.io/llms.txt`, `/node-operators/overview.md`, and `/chain-operators/guides/configuration/batcher.md` via two independent fetch pipelines; every request to docs.optimism.io returns 403 to non-browser clients from this environment (the session's egress gateway policy-denies the host, and the site's bot protection 403s the web-fetch pipeline — the whole host including `/` behaves the same, so this is not a missing-page signal). Corroboration used instead: web search confirms the docs reference `/llms.txt` as the complete documentation index, and the merged Option C plan records that the platform serves llms.txt and per-page `.md` natively. **Reviewer: please open https://docs.optimism.io/llms.txt and one `.md` page URL in a browser and confirm both render raw markdown.**
- **Hosted MCP endpoint:** availability on the current plan unconfirmed from this session → per the plan's fallback, the page leads with the llms.txt/markdown route and the hosted-MCP request is filed as ethereum-optimism/solutions#959.
- **External links:** the MCP reference fetch server path (`modelcontextprotocol/servers` → `src/fetch`) and its `uvx mcp-server-fetch` invocation verified against the live repo README.
- `docs.json` parses as valid JSON after the edit.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Browser check: `https://docs.optimism.io/llms.txt` and one per-page `.md` URL render raw markdown (see verification note above)
- [ ] Nav placement: "AI & Agents" beside Quickstart is the right Get-Started-adjacent position (C1's router may re-home it later)
- [ ] Prompt library: personas and page pairings read correctly; nothing over-promises
- [ ] MCP page makes no claims about a hosted endpoint we don't have

## Tracking

Tracks ethereum-optimism/solutions#958
Part of the serialized docs.json lane; will be rebased as earlier lane PRs merge.
